1 whole Canned Whole Peeled Tomatoes, Crushed
description: A stew made from flank steak, sofrito, and broth slowly simmered together in a crock pot until the meat softens to the point where it can be shredded with the backside of the fork.

name: Moroccan Meatballs
ingredients:
1 pound FOR THE MEATBALLS:
1 pinch Lean Ground Beef (I Used 95% Lean)
1 whole Salt
½ cups Medium Onion, Finely Diced
½ cups Fresh Parsley, Chopped
½ teaspoons Fresh Cilantro, Chopped
½ teaspoons Cumin
½ teaspoons Cinnamon

2 cloves FOR THE SAUCE:

2 whole Garlic, Minced Or Pressed
½ cups (28 Oz. Size) Crushed Or Ground Tomatoes

1 teaspoon Cumin
1 teaspoon Cinnamon

description: These Moroccan Meatballs are definitely a favorite meal in our house. The first time I made them, I felt like I was taking a bit of a risk. I knew I was a fan of spiced meats like this, but I had never made something myself with these spice combinations. I mean, cinnamon in meatballs? But I had a good feeling this recipe would be a winner, and it did not disappoint.

name: Moroccan Harira
ingredients:
1 Tablespoon FOR THE SPICE MIXTURE:

1  Water

name: Sweet Potato “Nachos”

1 whole Large Sweet Onion, Finely Diced

description: A simple appetizer made with sweet potatoes is sure to impress everyone who tastes it.

name: Pira Caldo

description: Pira caldo is a very hearty and nutritious soup that is rich in many different nutrients. Can be eaten as a standalone meal or as a starter to a very filling feast!

name: Marbled Red Velvet Cheesecake

1 whole FOR THE CAKE:

name: Chicken Artichoke French
ingredients:
1-½ cup FOR THE CHICKEN:
7  Milk
4 cups Eggs
1 teaspoon Bread Crumbs
1 teaspoon Garlic Powder
2 teaspoons Onion Powder

½ cups Lemon, Juiced, Plus More To Serve
description: Delicious and easy lemon-infused breaded chicken with artichokes.

name: Escarole with Currants, Pine Nuts, and Garlic
ingredients:
2 Tablespoons Olive Oil
6 cloves Garlic, Thinly Sliced
1 head (small) Escarole, Washed And Cut Into Bite-sized Pieces
2 Tablespoons Pine Nuts
3 Tablespoons Currants

A contrast of textures, colors and flavors make the best dishes, and I’m happy to say this Escarole with Currants, Pine Nuts, and Garlic does all that and more!

name: Chocolate Chip Cookies, Farm Boy-Style and Gluten-Free
ingredients:
1-⅔ cup Butter

name: Grapefruit Curd and Honeyed Yogurt Parfaits

name: Skillet Baked Eggplant and Zucchini Strips Parmigiana

description: Smoked honey is ridiculous good, with a deep grilled sticky sweet flavor that is perfect to use to glaze a ham or salmon, as an ingredient to pump up your smoky barbecue sauce (mmm ribs!), in a sweet and smoky vinaigrette or as a condiment, drizzled over fried chicken, pears or even ice cream. Endlessly useful, use it whenever you would use honey but want a little touch of outdoor smokeiness. If you have a smoker, you can probably smoke the honey that way, or if you are feel like a shortcut, you can probably just mix in some liquid smoke to any honey but I’m not a fan of liquid smoke. It comes across as chemically tasting to me (though perhaps I just haven’t tasted the right brand). Since I don’t have a smoker, I opted to tea smoke the honey, like I did with my tea-smoked shrimp, using rice, black tea and brown sugar. Just make sure you have your windows open or the hood over your stove is turned on when you make this. Otherwise you’re fire alarm is liable to go off!

Smoked honey is ridiculous good, with a deep grilled sticky sweet flavor that is perfect to use to glaze a ham or salmon, as an ingredient to pump up your smoky barbecue sauce (mmm ribs!), in a sweet and smoky vinaigrette or as a condiment, drizzled over fried chicken, pears or even ice cream. Endlessly useful, use it whenever you would use honey but want a little touch of outdoor smokeiness. If you have a smoker, you can probably smoke the honey that way, or if you are feel like a shortcut, you can probably just mix in some liquid smoke to any honey but I’m not a fan of liquid smoke. It comes across as chemically tasting to me (though perhaps I just haven’t tasted the right brand). Since I don’t have a smoker, I opted to tea smoke the honey, like I did with my tea-smoked shrimp, using rice, black tea and brown sugar. Just make sure you have your windows open or the hood over your stove is turned on when you make this. Otherwise you’re fire alarm is liable to go off!
